governanceNotes: D1 batch 64 (2026-09-26): identity deferred (MANIFESTATION-IDENTITY / DIRECTION-INVERSION with retinal-window duplication). Night blindness is a visual sign of upstream retinal and nutritional disease, and the located evidence supports no outgoing catalog edge: (i) the located literature (congenital stationary night blindness genotyping, CNGA1 and RP2 and rhodopsin retinitis-pigmentosa natural-history cohorts, RLBP1 patient-reported outcomes) documents natural history and function WITHIN the inherited retinal disease identities, so the direction runs retinal disease -> nyctalopia, not nyctalopia -> downstream condition; the published retinal-dystrophy to visual-impairment window already carries the visual-function pathway (identity-duplication guard; no evidence recycled from it per ME-29); (ii) candidate downstream outcomes - falls, fractures, driving compromise, depression, activity restriction - have zero located condition-specific quantification in populations indexed by nyctalopia; (iii) the vitamin A literature runs deficiency -> night blindness with intervention restoring pupillary responsiveness (direction-inversion guard for any nourishment edge), and vitamin A deficiency has no catalog identity to target in the reverse direction. Reopening conditions: (a) a cohort in which nyctalopia is the index finding with a catalog-fit secondary outcome quantified and retinal-disease severity, visual field, and comorbidity adjustment; or (b) a governance decision folding this sign into the retinal-dystrophy or retinitis identities as a symptom facet.
